title: Narrative Techniques: simile, contrast and personal voice
summary: يعني إيه simile وcontrast وpersonal voice، أمثلة من القطعة وأمثلة جديدة، وإزاي تكتب كل التأثيرات في سؤال Why does the author use…?

text: **Narrative techniques** are the tools a writer uses to make a story vivid and personal. In Unit 2 the book asks you to use three of them in your diary entry: a **simile**, **contrast** and **personal voice**.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن **أدوات الكاتب (narrative techniques)**، يعني الحاجات اللي الكاتب بيستخدمها علشان القصة تبقى **حيّة** ونحس بيها. في **Unit 2** (بعد القطعة الأدبية «Not Exactly a Relaxing Day») الكتاب بيطلب منك في **Diary Entry Checklist** تستخدم: **a simile, contrast, personal voice** ومعاهم narrative tenses وكلمات الدرس وreflection.
هنشرح كل أداة: **يعني إيه، إزاي تعرفها، أمثلة من القطعة، أمثلة جديدة، وتأثيرها (effect)**. وأهم حاجة: إزاي تجاوب سؤال **«Why does the author use ___?»**.

text: A **simile** compares two different things using **like**, **as … as** or **as if / as though**. It helps the reader imagine something clearly.

blocks.text: الـ **simile** يعني **تشبيه**: بنقارن حاجتين مختلفين باستخدام كلمة **like** (زي) أو **as … as** (… زي …) أو **as if / as though** (كأن). زي ما بنقول بالعربي: «عينيه **زي** البحر» أو «جري **كأنه** صاروخ».

rows: The road was **as hot as** an oven.
He cycled **as if** nothing had happened.

items.en: "a deep, physical tiredness that sat in my legs and shoulders **like warm sand**"
items.ar: شبّه التعب بـ **رملة دافية**: تقيلة، قاعدة في جسمه، بس **دافية ومريحة** شوية. يعني تعب بس مش وحش، فيه إحساس بالرضا.

items.en: "continued cycling **as if** the heat were simply decoration"
items.ar: صاحبه سايق **كأن** الحر ده مجرد ديكور، يعني مش فارق معاه خالص. ده بيبين الفرق بين خبرة الصاحب وضعف الراوي.

items.en: "**as if** … the distance were a minor detail"
items.ar: كأن المسافة حاجة صغيرة مش مهمة. بيأكد إن الصاحب شايفها سهلة.

items.en: After the match, my legs felt **like jelly**.
items.ar: رجليا بقت **زي الجيلي** = ضعيفة ومش ثابتة من التعب.

items.en: The pool was **as calm as glass** in the early morning.
items.ar: حمام السباحة كان هادي **زي الإزاز** = ساكن تمامًا.

items.en: I stared at my phone **as if** it were a magnet.
items.ar: كنت باصص للموبايل **كأنه** مغناطيس = مش قادر أبعد عنه (screen time).

items.en: The final kilometre stretched in front of me **like a never-ending ribbon**.
items.ar: آخر كيلو كان **زي شريطة ملهاش آخر** = حاسس إنه طويل جدًا.

items.en: Her paintbrush moved across the canvas **like a dancer**.
items.ar: الفرشة بتتحرك **زي راقصة** = بخفة وجمال (creative arts).

blocks.title: مش كل like تبقى simile!
items: ✗ I **like** cycling. ← ده فعل «بحب»، مش تشبيه.
✗ He looks **like** his brother. ← مقارنة بين حاجتين **من نفس النوع** (شخص وشخص)، ده مش simile أدبي.
✓ He ran **like the wind**. ← حاجتين **مختلفين** (إنسان وريح) = simile.
الـ **metaphor** (استعارة) من غير like/as: «My legs were **lead**.» ← ده مش simile.

blocks.text: **الـ effects بتاعة الـ simile (اكتب منها اللي ينفع في السؤال):**

items: helps the reader **picture / imagine** the scene or feeling clearly — يخلي القارئ يتخيل.
makes the description **vivid** and more **interesting** — يخلي الوصف حي.
explains an **abstract feeling** (like tiredness) through something **concrete** we know — يوضح إحساس صعب بحاجة نعرفها.
**emphasises** a quality (how heavy, how easy, how hot) — يأكد صفة.
shows the narrator's **feelings or attitude** — يبين مشاعر الراوي.
creates a **mood** (calm, tense, humorous) — يعمل جو معين.
can add **humour** — ممكن يضحّك (زي «the heat were simply decoration»).

text: **Contrast** means putting two opposite things next to each other: before and after, easy and hard, calm and tense. It makes the difference stand out and shows change.

blocks.text: الـ **contrast** يعني إنك تحط **حاجتين عكس بعض** جنب بعض: قبل وبعد، سهل وصعب، هادي ومتوتر، أنا وصاحبي. الهدف إن **الفرق يبان** وإننا نحس **بالتغيير**. كلمات بتدل عليه: **but, however, while, whereas, then, instead, although, at first … by the end**.

items.en: **Home vs the Nile trip:** "complete stillness" on the sofa ↔ cycling for hours in the sun.
items.ar: الراحة في البيت قصاد المجهود في الرحلة. ده تضاد في **فكرة الـ leisure**.

items.en: **The sun:** "gentle and golden at dawn" ↔ "stronger and more direct".
items.ar: الشمس الحلوة الصبح قصاد الشمس القوية بعدين = بيبين إن اليوم **اتقلب**.

items.en: **The friend vs the narrator:** the friend cycles easily ↔ "I struggled to keep up."
items.ar: صاحبه مرتاح وهو بيعاني = بيأكد **تعبه**.

items.en: **The ending:** "exhausted" ↔ "strangely satisfied".
items.ar: تعبان **و**راضي في نفس الوقت = الإحساس معقد ومختلط.

items.en: **Before vs after:** leisure = doing nothing ↔ leisure can come "from effort".
items.ar: فكرته في الأول قصاد فكرته في الآخر = **اتغير واتعلم**.

items.en: **At first**, I spent my evenings scrolling. **By the end of the month**, I was painting every night.
items.ar: قبل وبعد = تغيير في العادات.

items.en: **While** my brother found chess boring, I found it exciting.
items.ar: شخصين وكل واحد له رأي = while.

items.en: The gym was noisy and crowded, **whereas** the park was silent and empty.
items.ar: مكانين عكس بعض = whereas.

items.en: I expected a lazy afternoon. **Instead**, I climbed a mountain.
items.ar: المتوقع قصاد اللي حصل = instead.

items: **highlights the difference** between two things — يبرز الفرق.
shows a **change** in the narrator's feelings or ideas — يبين التغيير.
creates **surprise** or **tension** — يعمل مفاجأة أو توتر.
makes the **message** clearer (comfort vs challenge) — يوضح الرسالة.
makes the reader **compare** and think — يخلي القارئ يقارن ويفكر.
can show **irony** (what we expect vs what happens) — يبين المفارقة.

text: **Personal voice** is the writer's own way of speaking to the reader. It uses the **first person** (I, me, my), honest feelings, private thoughts, questions to oneself and a natural, sometimes humorous style.

blocks.text: الـ **personal voice** يعني الكاتب بيكلمك **كأنه صاحبك**: بيستخدم **I / me / my**، بيقول **مشاعره بصراحة**، بيعترف بضعفه، بيسأل نفسه، وأسلوبه **طبيعي** وأحيانًا فيه **خفة دم**. ده عكس الكتابة الرسمية الباردة. الكتاب في Unit 8 كمان بيقول: «Use the first person (I, my, me) to share your thoughts and experiences.»

rows: "I was genuinely curious whether I could finish"
"That day changed my understanding of leisure."
"My legs ached. My breathing was uneven."

items.en: I'll be honest: I hated the first swimming lesson.
items.ar: اعتراف صريح + I = personal voice.

items.en: Was I scared? Of course I was.
items.ar: بيسأل نفسه ويجاوب = قريب من القارئ.

items.en: My phone, my faithful friend, stayed in my bag all day, and I survived!
items.ar: خفة دم + مشاعر = صوت شخصي.

items.en: I still don't know why I agreed, but I'm glad I did.
items.ar: تفكير داخلي وتأمل.

items: makes the story feel **real and believable** — القصة تبان حقيقية.
builds a **close relationship** with the reader — يقرّب القارئ من الراوي.
helps the reader **share / understand the narrator's feelings** — نحس باللي هو حاسه.
shows the narrator's **personality** (honest, funny, lazy, proud) — يبين شخصيته.
makes the narrator **likeable** because he admits weakness — نحبه لأنه صريح.
makes the **lesson / reflection** more convincing — الدرس في الآخر يقنعنا أكتر.

blocks.text: قاعدة المدرس: إزاي تجاوب «Why does the author use ___?»

text: When the question asks **why** the writer uses a technique, name the technique, quote it briefly, then give **all the possible effects** that fit the example.

blocks.text: لما يسألك **«Why does the author use a simile / contrast / personal voice in line X?»** اكتب **كل الـ effects الممكنة** اللي تنفع مع المثال، مش effect واحد. الخطوات:

items: **سمّي الأداة:** The writer uses a **simile** …
**اقتبس كلمتين:** … "like warm sand" …
**اشرح المعنى في جملة:** … to compare his tiredness to warm, heavy sand.
**اكتب كل التأثيرات:** to help the reader imagine…, to make the description vivid…, to emphasise…, to show his feelings…, to create a mood…

blocks.title: Model answer: "Why does the author use a simile in 'like warm sand'?"
blocks.task: Why does the author use a simile in the phrase "like warm sand"?
text: The author uses a simile, "like warm sand", to compare the narrator's tiredness to heavy, warm sand sitting in his legs and shoulders. The simile helps the reader to imagine exactly how his body felt. It makes the description vivid and turns an abstract feeling, tiredness, into something concrete that we can almost touch. It emphasises how heavy and deep his exhaustion was. At the same time, the word "warm" suggests a pleasant, comforting feeling, so the simile shows that his tiredness was mixed with satisfaction. Finally, it creates a calm, peaceful mood at the end of the story.
notes: كتبنا **كل التأثيرات**: imagine، vivid، abstract → concrete، emphasise، feelings (warm = satisfaction)، mood.

rows: but / however / while / then / at first … by the end

blocks.title: استخدمهم في الـ Diary Entry
items: **Simile** في النهاية علشان توصف تعبك أو فرحتك (الكتاب بيقول كده في The ending).
**Contrast** بين أول اليوم وآخره، أو بينك وبين صاحبك.
**Personal voice**: اكتب بـ I، اعترف بخوفك أو كسلك، اسأل نفسك سؤال.
متحطش 10 similes! واحد أو اتنين حلوين أحسن.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء
items: ✗ تكتب effect واحد عام: «to make it interesting» وبس ← ✓ اكتب **كل** الـ effects اللي تنفع.
✗ تقول simile لـ «I like cycling» ← ✓ like هنا فعل.
✗ تسمي contrast «comparison» وخلاص ← ✓ قول **contrast** ووضّح **الحاجتين العكس**.
✗ تفتكر personal voice يعني «بيستخدم I» بس ← ✓ كمان المشاعر، الصراحة، الأسئلة، خفة الدم.
✗ تنقل الجملة كلها ← ✓ اقتباس كلمتين أو تلاتة.

items.q: 1. "He cycled as if the heat were simply decoration."
2. "The sun, which had been gentle and golden at dawn, grew stronger."
3. "Perhaps it was pride … Or perhaps it was something less comfortable to admit."
4. "I was exhausted … But I was also strangely satisfied."
5. My heart was beating like a drum before the race.
6. I'll admit it: I was jealous of my friend's energy.
7. Last year I hated sport, whereas now I can't live without it.

8. Which sentence contains a simile?
a. I like painting.  b. She looks like her mother.  c. The lake was as still as a mirror.  d. I feel tired.

9. The main effect of contrasting the narrator with his friend is to ______.
a. show the friend is lazy  b. emphasise how much the narrator struggled  c. describe the Nile  d. end the story

10. Personal voice makes the extract ______.
a. formal and distant  b. real and close to the reader  c. scientific  d. shorter

11. Which linking word does NOT usually show contrast?
a. however  b. whereas  c. because  d. instead

blocks.text: **تالتًا: Why does the author use ___? (اكتب كل التأثيرات)**

items.q: 12. Why does the author use the simile "as if the heat were simply decoration"?
items.a: To compare the heat to harmless decoration and show that the friend did not notice it. It **emphasises** how experienced and strong the friend was, **contrasts** him with the suffering narrator, adds **humour**, and helps the reader **imagine** the scene. It may also show the narrator's **feeling** of frustration that his friend finds it so easy.

items.q: 13. Why does the author contrast the sun "at dawn" with the sun later in the morning?
items.a: To **show the change** from a pleasant start to a difficult ride, to **create tension**, to **highlight** how the conditions became harder, and to mirror the change in the narrator's **mood** from relaxed to uncertain.

items.q: 14. Why does the author use short sentences such as "My legs ached. My breathing was uneven."?
items.a: To show the narrator's **personal**, physical suffering, to make the reader **feel** his tiredness, to slow the pace and create **tension**, to make the moment **dramatic**, and to make it sound like **real, honest** thoughts.

items.q: 15. Why does the author use personal voice throughout the extract?
items.a: To make the story **real and believable**, to build a **close link** with the reader, to let us **share his feelings**, to show his **personality** (honest, a little lazy, proud), to add **humour**, and to make the final **lesson** more convincing.

items.q: 16. Why does the author begin with the narrator's love of staying at home?
items.a: To create a **contrast** with the hard trip, to show how much he **changes**, to make the ending more **surprising**, and to make the **message** about leisure clearer.

items.q: 17. Write a simile to describe how you feel after a long exam.
items.a: مثال: My brain felt **like an empty battery**. — تشبيه التعب الذهني ببطارية فاضية.

items.q: 18. Write a simile about a crowded place.
items.a: مثال: The market was **as busy as a beehive**.

items.q: 19. Write two sentences that show contrast between your screen time before and after a change.
items.a: مثال: **At first**, I spent six hours a day on my phone. **Now**, I spend that time reading and playing football.

items.q: 20. Rewrite in a personal voice: "The walk was long and the walker was tired."
items.a: مثال: **Honestly, I thought that walk would never end. My feet were begging me to stop!**

items.q: 21. Write a short diary opening (2-3 sentences) using all three techniques.
items.a: مثال: Dear Diary, I thought today would be easy. **Instead**, the hike was **like climbing a wall**. **I'll be honest: I nearly cried!**

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: **Simile** = تشبيه بـ like / as … as / as if ← يخلي القارئ يتخيل، يأكد صفة، يوضح الإحساس، يعمل mood.
**Contrast** = حاجتين عكس بعض ← يبرز الفرق، يبين التغيير، يعمل مفاجأة أو توتر، يوضح الرسالة.
**Personal voice** = I + مشاعر + صراحة ← القصة حقيقية وقريبة ونفهم الشخصية.
سؤال **Why does the author use ___?** = سمّي الأداة + اقتبس كلمتين + اشرح + **اكتب كل التأثيرات**.
